agents.name: Jerry
agents.summary: Read alpha.py (3 lines). Extracted one documented invariant from a comment: total(values) sums all values, including negative values. The implementation is a single `return sum(values)`, which uses Python's built-in sum and therefore adds every element of the iterable, including negative numeric values. Verdict for the sole invariant: PASS.
agents.review_summary: Independently read alpha.py. The file contains exactly three lines: a comment documenting one invariant ('# Sum all values, including negative values.'), a function definition, and 'return sum(values)'. The submitted result correctly extracted that single invariant and correctly marked it PASS based on Python's built-in sum semantics. All acceptance criteria are met: actual source was read, exact lines are quoted with line numbers, and a per-invariant verdict is provided.

agents.name: Addison
agents.summary: beta.py contains exactly one documented invariant in a comment: 'Count unique values, preserving case distinctions.' The implementation is def count(values): return len(set(values)). This satisfies the invariant because set(values) deduplicates the input and Python's set equality/hashing for strings is case-sensitive, so 'A' and 'a' remain distinct. No additional invariants were documented in a docstring or comments.
agents.review_summary: The submitted audit accurately reflects beta.py. Independent read_file confirmed the file contains exactly three lines: a comment on line 1 stating 'Count unique values, preserving case distinctions.', a function definition on line 2, and 'return len(set(values))' on line 3. The submitted per-invariant verdict of pass is correct for the documented invariant because set(values) deduplicates by equality, and Python string equality/hashing is case-sensitive, so 'A' and 'a' remain distinct. No additional documented invariants are present in beta.py.
